title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented University of Arizona rituals and recurring expressions of Wildcat spirit.

cards.title: Say “Bear Down!”
cards.subtitle: University-wide Wildcat rallying cry
cards.notes: Use the university’s official motto as a greeting or cheer at an appropriate campus or athletics gathering; its origin is tied to John “Button” Salmon.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Arizona identifies “Bear Down” as its official motto and an enduring rallying cry originating with John Byrd “Button” Salmon in 1926.
cards.access_notes: No special access is inherent to using the motto; follow event rules when cheering.

cards.title: Listen for “Bear Down, Arizona”
cards.subtitle: University fight song
cards.notes: Listen for the song at an Arizona sporting event or from the campus bell tower, then join only if you know the words and event etiquette allows.
cards.short_summary: The fight song built from Arizona’s signature phrase.
cards.evidence_claim: Arizona Alumni reports that Jack K. Lee wrote “Bear Down, Arizona,” and that it is played at University of Arizona sporting events and from the campus bell tower daily.
cards.access_notes: Sporting-event entry rules apply; bell-tower play is heard from public campus areas.

cards.title: Catch the second fight song
cards.subtitle: Arizona athletics and bell-tower music
cards.notes: Notice the companion song, “Fight, Wildcats, Fight,” during athletics programming or bell-tower play; it is distinct from “Bear Down, Arizona.”
cards.short_summary: Arizona’s other regularly played fight song.
cards.evidence_claim: Arizona Alumni states that Douglas Holsclaw’s “Fight, Wildcats, Fight” is played throughout University of Arizona sporting events and from the campus bell tower daily.
cards.access_notes: Sporting-event entry rules apply; bell-tower play is heard from public campus areas.

cards.title: See the Salmon-bust tribute
cards.subtitle: Near Lowell-Stevens Football Facility
cards.notes: Before a home football game, watch the team’s tribute at John “Button” Salmon’s bust; keep clear of the team procession and facility operations.
cards.short_summary: Football players touch Salmon’s bust before home games.
cards.evidence_claim: Arizona Alumni documents that, since 2013, Arizona football players pass and touch John “Button” Salmon’s bust while completing the Wildcat Walk before every home game.
cards.access_notes: View only from areas open to the public on home-game days; respect event and team-route controls.

cards.title: Line up for the Wildcat Walk
cards.subtitle: Cherry Avenue route to Arizona Stadium
cards.notes: Before a home football game, use public viewing areas along the announced route to greet the arriving team, band, cheerleaders, and mascots.
cards.short_summary: A pregame procession from the Mall to Arizona Stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: Arizona Athletics introduced the Wildcat Walk as a game-day tradition in which the football team, Pride of Arizona, cheerleaders, and mascots proceed down Cherry Avenue toward Arizona Stadium.
cards.source_title: Wildcats to Debut New Game Day Tradition
cards.access_notes: Occurs before Arizona home football games; use designated public areas and follow current game-day instructions.

cards.title: Watch “A” Mountain light up
cards.subtitle: Sentinel Peak during Homecoming
cards.notes: During Homecoming programming, view the red-lit “A” from a lawful public vantage point; do not approach the lighting operation or restricted terrain.
cards.short_summary: Homecoming begins with a red flare-lit “A” on Sentinel Peak.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Arizona News describes the traditional lighting of “A” Mountain with red flares as the kickoff of Homecoming festivities and Spirit Week.
cards.source_title: Desert Bound: Celebrating Wildcat pride during Spirit Week and Homecoming
cards.access_notes: Scheduled as part of Homecoming/Spirit Week; view from lawful public spaces and follow fire-safety directions.

cards.title: Join Homecoming week
cards.subtitle: Annual University of Arizona reunion tradition
cards.notes: Check the university’s Homecoming schedule for public programs that fit your interests, then attend the listed campus or community events as directed.
cards.short_summary: A University of Arizona tradition dating to 1914.
cards.evidence_claim: Arizona Alumni states that University of Arizona Homecoming dates to 1914 and was suspended only during World War I and World War II.
cards.access_notes: Events and access vary by the annual Homecoming schedule.

cards.title: Follow the Territorial Cup
cards.subtitle: Arizona–Arizona State football rivalry trophy
cards.notes: Follow the annual Arizona–Arizona State football matchup and learn the trophy’s long history before taking part in any official game-day programming.
cards.short_summary: The trophy tradition reaches back to Arizona’s first football season.
cards.evidence_claim: Arizona Alumni states that the Territorial Cup tradition goes back to 1899, the year the University of Arizona first fielded a football team.
cards.access_notes: Game attendance and related events are subject to current ticketing and venue rules.

cards.title: Spot both Wildcats
cards.subtitle: University of Arizona’s paired mascots
cards.notes: Look for Wilbur and Wilma at their respective athletics appearances, and enjoy the performance without trying to identify the student performers.
cards.short_summary: Arizona’s mascot tradition features a married Wildcat pair.
cards.evidence_claim: Arizona Alumni documents that Wilbur and Wilma met in 1986 and were married before the Arizona State football game that year; their performer identities remain secret until the final regular-season home basketball game.
cards.access_notes: Mascot appearances depend on the athletics schedule and venue rules.

cards.title: Meet up at Bear Down Friday
cards.subtitle: Main Gate Square before home football games
cards.notes: Before a home football game, check current event details for the Main Gate Square gathering, including the Pride of Arizona march-through and spirit programming.
cards.short_summary: A pregame Friday gathering centered on Wildcat cheers.
cards.evidence_claim: Arizona Athletics identifies Bear Down Friday at Main Gate Square as a ZonaZoo event before home football games, featuring the Pride of Arizona, Arizona Athletics speakers, Pomline, Wilbur, and Wilma.
cards.access_notes: Arizona Athletics says this occurs the day before home football games; confirm current event details before going.
